n299/README.md and #1031 describe the construction: diagonal slices, each filled from a reflected or translated copy of a public packing, the outer slices from 372 squares and the seven middle slices from 335 squares, both from Asterios Panoras's public Kaggle compilation (version 17), which Kaggle's community explorer (nevska) links to prvsiyan's notebook 'A Square Deal' (372) and to four notebooks with the same score, by areebbb, jazivxt, alexchilton and prvsiyan (335); then a local optimization exchanging the separating edges of touching pairs, and a reflection of part of one tilted group across the diagonal x + y = S with its neighbours released, which gave the final gain; 55 squares tilt at least 15 degrees one way and 54 the other. They say no test of local optimality was run and no optimality is claimed. It asks for credit to Joost de Winter, Delft University of Technology, after the 335- and 372-square packings in Panoras's compilation (prvsiyan, areebbb, jazivxt, alexchilton).

verify_exact.py (separating axes) and check_area.py (the area of each close pair's clipped intersection), Python's fractions.Fraction and its standard library only, are the folder's two exact checkers; #1031 says each reports 299 squares and 714 close pairs, that they share no code but have one author and read the same input file, and that the witness has not yet been run through this repository's checker. #1031 and n299/README.md say the search, optimization and rational certificate were produced with GPT-6.2 Sol (OpenAI) and the repository files, checks and figure with Claude (Anthropic), both under his direction. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.
